overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post notice of its March 5, 2024 meeting to the municipal website; no violation for April 11, 2023 because no meeting occurred; minutes claim declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to properly post notice of an April 11, 2023 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, where no meeting occurred, the Board could not violate the Open Meeting Law by either failing to post notice or posting an insufficient notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to properly post notice of its March 5, 2024 meeting; notice was faxed to the Town Clerk but never posted to the municipal website.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post notice of its March 5, 2024, meeting to the municipal website, the official posting location for all public bodies in the Town of Yarmouth.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant alleged the March 5, 2024 minutes were insufficient because they contain no dialogue; this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review its merits.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All members of the Board attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by the Attorney General's office within 90 days.
The Board certify to the Attorney General's office that each Board member has completed the webinar training within 95 days.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order all members of the Board to attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by our office within the next 90 days.
